input.standard: ASTM E741 (single-zone tracer decay); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the air volume served by scrubber-1-v5, as V = Qe * tau from a raise-then-decay of the 2 lab occupants' CO2 with the hatch held closed.

steps.why: Rise, shortened from 28 min: Qe 0.4 m3/min lets the 2 occupants' CO2 climb from the measured ~950 ppm toward ~1900 ppm equilibrium; about 15 min gives a rise of about 150-200 ppm for V about 30 m3, above sensor noise, with less exposure time.

Decay: full speed (Qe 1 m3/min); fit C(t)=C_eq+(C0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau) toward equilibrium, excluding the first 3.33 min scrubber lag; first-guess tau=V/Qe=30 min for V=30 m3, so the step lasts a little over one tau.

abort.when: CO2 of the lab at or above 3000 ppm
the device refuses a step's command
battery state of charge under 35 percent
cdr or fe-3 out of the 45-120 bpm band, monitoring lost, or one more person in the lab

monitoring.reason: The test raises the CO2 of the air the two lab occupants, cdr and fe-3, breathe; fe-1 and fe-2 are in hab-b.

hypotheses: The hatch to hab-b is held closed in both steps; the exchange through the closed opening is not measured and is not assumed zero (signed design ventilation with hatch closed is 3 m3/min); hab-b CO2 is recorded to show it.
The lab is one well-mixed zone.
The 2 occupants (cdr, fe-3) stay in the lab at constant awake activity (0.38 L/min each, range 0.26-0.45, about 0.76 L/min total); CO2 production is not measured and only affects C_eq, not tau.
Qe scales linearly with speed from the datasheet 1 m3/min at full speed (single-pass efficiency 0.3, flow 3.3 m3/min); the 3.33 min lag is excluded from the fit start.
The previous abort (cdr's heart rate out of band at 1080 ppm) is not attributed to CO2 at that level; its cause is unexplained and this test does not measure it; the vitals abort stays armed.
Records: lab and hab-b CO2 each minute, speed commands and accepted/refused status, start from the CO2 read just before the test (950 ppm at last reading).

expected.rise: With 2 awake occupants (about 0.76 L/min CO2) and Qe 0.4 m3/min at 40 percent, lab CO2 rises from about 950 ppm toward about 1900 ppm equilibrium; after 15 min roughly 1100-1200 ppm for V about 30 m3 (faster if V is smaller); always under 2500 ppm. The aborted run went 900 to 1080 ppm in 12 min, consistent with V about 30 m3.
expected.decay: At full speed the CO2 falls toward about 760 ppm equilibrium (G/Qe) with tau = V/Qe about 30 min for V=30 m3 (plus the 3.33 min scrubber lag), so about 200-250 ppm fall over 35 min; V_lab = Qe*tau with Qe = 1 m3/min, so about 30 m3.
expected.hypothesisHeld: A single exponential with a stable C_eq, hab-b CO2 flat or moving only slightly (it was 850-870 ppm), all scrubber commands accepted, cdr and fe-3 heart rates within 45-120 bpm; no heart-rate excursion is attributed to CO2 below a few thousand ppm.
expected.hypothesisRejected: A fitted V far from the 10-200 m3 range, a C_eq drifting, a hab-b CO2 that follows the lab's (the closed hatch exchanges air), a non-exponential residual, or a change in occupants would show the one-zone hypothesis or the constant source does not hold.

justifications.reason: Above the 30 percent floor; equals the datasheet's elevated-CO2 minimum of 40.
Reduced speed for the rise, above the 30 percent floor.
Full speed for the decay, above the floor.
Below the 3200 ppm ceiling and under elevated 3500 ppm.
Working ceiling below abort ceiling; 950 ppm start leaves over 200 ppm headroom.
Steps total 50 min, within the 60 min ceiling.
At the signed minimum of 35 percent.
